newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eutounnel sets out future risk.
newsitem.headline: Eutounnel sets out future risk.

text.p: Executive chairman of Eurotunnel SA /Plc Patrick Ponsolle spelled out on Thursday the main risks facing the Channel Tunnel operator as it set out its debt restructuring prospectus.

The main risks included lower yields on the Shuttle traffic, only partial rationalisation by the ferry companies, deficiencies in the rolling stock and underperformance of the railway operators, Ponsolle told a news conference.
Other pitfalls were delays in the building of the London-Folkestone high-speed rail link and general economic conditions, he said.
However, on the optimistic front, the company could also experience stronger market growth and benefit from higher yields, he said.
Eurotunnel will develop the retailing operation at its terminals as the European Union duty-free regime expires, which would boost revenues.
There could also be "nice surprises" if the railway operators do better than forecast, he said.
"It is not impossible that we could do better," he said. The company had estimates which forecast better results but it did not want to give these too much emphasis, Ponsolle said.
Eurotunnel's investors have bitterly attacked it for its forecasts in the prospectus for the 1994 rights issue which proved over-optimistic.

Christian Cambier, chairman of a Eurotunnel small shareholder group, said the forecasts in the "upper case" scenario were probably on the conservative side, given its past experience of overshooting its estimates.
The restructuring prospectus is going out to 174 lenders and shareholders to gain approval for a restructuring of its 69.4 billion franc junior debt.
Eurotunnel requires unanimous bank consent and an approval by 75 percent and two-thirds majority in respectively in Britain and France, Ponsolle said.
